claims.text: Increasing configurational entropy tunes local lattice distortions.
Increasing configurational entropy tunes electron–phonon coupling.
Lattice inhomogeneity from mixing several principal elements creates locally enhanced pairing interactions.
The locally enhanced pairing interactions can overcome disorder scattering and produce superconductivity.
The as-synthesized high-entropy alloy has random atomic-site occupancy.
The as-synthesized high-entropy alloy has a disordered crystalline lattice.
Using four or five elements increases configurational entropy relative to using fewer elements.
High configurational entropy produces local lattice distortion and inhomogeneity.
The entropy-induced lattice distortion modifies the phonon spectrum.
The entropy-induced lattice distortion modifies the local electronic density of states.
Chemical and structural disorder enhances electron–phonon coupling by creating favorable lattice strains.
Within an optimal disorder window, enhanced electron–phonon coupling increases electron pairing interactions.
Optimized configurational entropy improves superconducting critical parameters relative to a more uniform alloy.
The high-entropy sample will exhibit zero electrical resistance and a diamagnetic response in the 2–20 K test regime.
The high-entropy sample will have a higher and/or sharper superconducting transition than the low-entropy control.
Increasing configurational entropy can enhance critical current density.
Increasing configurational entropy may increase superconducting volume fraction.
The low-entropy control may show no superconductivity or a lower, less robust superconducting response.
Excessive disorder suppresses superconductivity, so enhancement occurs only in an optimal configurational-entropy window.
The proposed mechanism applies broadly to similar multi-principal-element alloys under low-temperature conditions.
